events.text: Objective: Determine whether Winterhalter Gastronom GmbH should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current commercial dishwashers and glasswashers, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeframe for any proposed experiment.; Current reach to individual buyers is unknown; must be discovered.; Any investment must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and ability to capture value.; Alternatives include product redesign, new distribution route, targeting a different customer group, or no expansion.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home kitchen dishwashers) with dedicated branding, marketing, and sales channels.; 2) Expand the existing commercial product line into adjacent consumer segments without differentiation (e.g., add a consumer‑grade glasswasher).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial dishwashers and glasswashers, possibly deepening existing B2B relationships.; 4) Change the route to buyers: partner with retailers or online platforms to reach consumers directly, leveraging existing distribution networks.; 5) Target a different customer group: shift focus to small restaurants, cafes, or hotel chains rather than large commercial facilities..

Test "Premium vs Eco‑friendly Under‑counter Dishwasher Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenario. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a premium‑priced under‑counter dishwasher described as compact, space‑saving, and high‑quality. Group B sees the same product described as eco‑friendly, emphasizing water and energy savings. Both groups see a standard consumer dishwasher as a baseline. Participants indicate whether they would purchase the product and, if so, at what price they would pay.. Sample: 300 homeowners (150 per group) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would purchase) and maximum price willingness to pay (continuous).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between Group A and Group B is at least 10 percentage points (e.g., Group A ≥ 60% and Group B ≤ 50%), we conclude the premium positioning (T1) is more effective. If the difference is at least 10 percentage points in favor of the eco‑friendly positioning (Group B ≥ 60% and Group A ≤ 50%), we conclude the eco‑friendly positioning (T2) is more effective. If neither difference reaches the 10‑point threshold, we conclude neither positioning is significantly more effective.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home kitchen dishwashers) that emphasizes premium compact design, space savings, and high-quality integration. Use the existing UC‑series configurability to create a consumer‑grade product that can be marketed through retail or online channels. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home kitchen dishwashers) that emphasizes premium compact design, space savings, and high-quality integration. Use the existing UC‑series configurability to create a consumer‑grade product that can be marketed through retail or online channels. Target customer: Homeowners with limited kitchen space who need a reliable dishwasher but cannot fit a full‑size machine.. Value proposition: A compact, under‑counter dishwasher that integrates seamlessly into modern kitchens, offering space savings, high quality, and the flexibility to customize as a glasswasher, dishwasher, or bistro warewasher.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Premium vs Eco‑friendly Under‑counter Dishwasher Test (or a smaller pilot) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for the premium positioning versus the eco‑friendly positioning.. Uncertainty: The actual willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a compact under‑counter dishwasher is unknown. Additionally, the competitive landscape and the effectiveness of eco‑friendly messaging are uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows the eco‑friendly positioning generates significantly higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than the premium positioning, we would shift focus to sustainability messaging.; If neither positioning achieves the 10‑percentage‑point threshold, we would reconsider the investment and explore alternative consumer propositions or distribution channels.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Premium Positioning Test for Home Office vs Home Consumer" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to a premium-priced home office machine versus a standard consumer machine. Participants are recruited from home office workers and home coffee enthusiasts. Each participant sees one of the two machine descriptions and is asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants: 150 home office workers and 150 home coffee enthusiasts, balanced across gender and age. Recruitment via online panels to ensure diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each machine description.. Predictions: T1: Home office participants will show purchase intent at least 20 points higher for the premium-priced home office machine than for the standard consumer machine.; T2: Home coffee enthusiasts will show purchase intent at least 20 points higher for the premium-priced home consumer machine than for the standard consumer machine.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the premium home office machine and the standard consumer machine is at least 20 points in favor of the premium home office machine, proceed to develop a differentiated home office proposition. If the difference in purchase intent between the premium home consumer machine and the standard consumer machine is at least 20 points in favor of the premium home consumer machine, proceed to develop a differentiated home consumer proposition. If neither difference meets the 20‑point threshold, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and continue focusing on existing professional machines.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home office users, leveraging Franke’s professional brand and premium positioning. Conduct the proposed Premium Positioning Test to validate demand before full development. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home office users, leveraging Franke’s professional brand and premium positioning. Conduct the proposed Premium Positioning Test to validate demand before full development. Target customer: Home office workers and small business owners who value quality coffee and a professional aesthetic in their workspace.. Value proposition: A premium-priced home office coffee machine that positions Franke as a professional-grade brand, offering superior taste, convenience, and a professional aesthetic to enhance productivity and work experience.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the Premium Positioning Test (300 participants, 12 weeks, €20,000) to measure purchase intent differences between premium home office and standard consumer machines. Use the 20‑point threshold to decide whether to proceed with a full‑f‑. Uncertainty: The willingness of home office consumers to pay a premium for a professional‑grade machine is uncertain. The test will clarify whether demand exists and is large enough to justify investment.. Would change if: If the Premium Positioning Test shows purchase intent for the premium home office machine is at least 20 points lower than for the standard consumer machine, we would abandon the differentiated home office proposition and continue focusing; evidence_ids. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Specialized vs Lifestyle Glove Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to two product concepts: (1) Specialized glove for outdoor recreation (e.g., durable, waterproof, stylish design) and (2) Lifestyle-branded glove aligned with personal style and values. Participants will be randomly assigned to view one concept and then asked about willingness to pay a premium, purchase intent, and likelihood to recommend.. Sample: 500 adult consumers aged 18-45, recruited via an online panel, balanced across gender and geographic regions to ensure diversity.. Measure: 1) Willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay at least 20% more than standard industrial gloves). 2) Purchase intent (percentage indicating they would buy the product). 3) Recommendation likelihood (percentage indicating they would recommend the product to a friend).. Predictions: T1: Higher willingness to pay premium and purchase intent for the specialized glove compared to the lifestyle-branded glove.; T2: Higher willingness to pay premium and purchase intent for the lifestyle-branded glove compared to the specialized glove.. Decision rule: If the specialized glove achieves at least 30% willingness to pay premium and at least 20% purchase intent, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition for outdoor recreation. If the lifestyle-branded glove achieves at least 30% willingness to pay premium and at least 20% purchase intent, proceed to develop a lifestyle-branded consumer proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand into consumer markets.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Test "Precision vs Health Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants view one of two product descriptions for a digital kitchen scale: Precision (accurate, fraction-of-a-gram measurement) or Health (portion control, carbohydrate counting). They are then asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay (EUR).. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and age. Randomly assigned to see Precision or Health description.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for Precision description.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for Health description.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay for Precision is at least 20% higher than for Health, proceed with a precision‑focused consumer proposition. Test "Consumer Proposition Test: Convenience vs Sustainability Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product offers. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: (A) convenience-focused message emphasizing small-space cleaning and time savings; (B) sustainability-focused message emphasizing eco-friendly features and water savings. Both conditions present the same product (a consumer‑focused version of a professional scrubber). Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not likely, 7‑very likely) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 U.S. adults aged 25‑55 who have cleaned a home in the past year, recruited via an online panel. Randomly assigned 250 to Condition A and 250 to Condition B.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑90) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Condition A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for Condition A is at least 1.5 points higher than Condition B (i.e., Condition A ≥ 5.5), conclude that convenience messaging drives purchase and recommend developing a differentiated consumer proposition focused on small‑space convenience. If Condition B ≥ 5.5, conclude sustainability messaging drives purchase and recommend a sustainability‑focused proposition. If the difference is ≤ 1.5, indicate inconclusive results and suggest further testing.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Convenience vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A (convenience-focused) or Condition B (energy-efficiency-focused). Both conditions present a countertop ice maker with identical features (e.g., nugget ice, compact design, easy refilling). Participants are asked to indicate their primary purchase reason (convenience vs cost savings) and willingness to pay a premium.. Sample: 500 residential consumers (aged 25-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two conditions.. Measure: Primary purchase reason (convenience vs cost savings) and willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay at least 10% more than a standard commercial unit).. Predictions: T1: Condition A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Condition A.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the two conditions is at least 10 percentage points and the condition with the higher intent is the convenience-focused one, proceed with a differentiated consumer proposition emphasizing convenience. If the difference is less than 10 points and the energy-efficiency condition wins, pursue an energy-efficiency-focused proposition. If both conditions are equal, do not invest in a differentiated proposition at this time.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Test "Precision vs Health Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants view one of two product descriptions for a digital kitchen scale: Precision (accurate, fraction-of-a-gram measurement) or Health (portion control, carbohydrate counting). They are then asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay (EUR).. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and dietary interest (e.g., low-carb, keto).. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Precision messaging will generate higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Health messaging.; T2: Health messaging will generate higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Precision messaging.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay for Precision messaging is at least 20% above the average willingness to pay for Health messaging, proceed with a precision‑focused consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 20%, proceed with a health‑focused proposition. If both differences are within 20% of each other, do not commit to either proposition and conduct further market research.. Cost: 8000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Consumer Preference Test: Convenience vs Sustainability" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Group A sees a description of a compact, high-performance scrubber marketed as convenient for small spaces and tight budgets. Group B sees the same product described as sustainable, eco-friendly, and water-efficient. Both groups see price points and a call-to-action to purchase. The test measures purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (maximum price).. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two groups (150 per group). Recruitment targets homeowners and small business owners with limited space.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and maximum willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary measure: stated primary purchase driver (convenience vs sustainability).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If Group A purchase intent exceeds Group B by at least 10 percentage points and its average willingness to pay is at least 20% higher, conclude T1 is supported. If Group B purchase intent exceeds Group A by at least 10 percentage points and its average willingness to pay is at least 20% higher, conclude T2 is supported. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience, small-space performance, and budget-friendly pricing. Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Trust vs Status Framing" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners interested in home safety. They view a product description of the Dräger Alcotest 4000 breathalyzer. Half see a trust‑framing message emphasizing professional police/fire‑service use and safety credentials. The other half see a status‑framing message emphasizing premium design, professional-grade quality, and exclusivity. Both groups are offered a fixed price of €334.44. The test measures purchase intent (binary: "Would you buy this product?") and willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7‑point scale.. Sample: Proposed sample: 400 homeowners (200 per condition) from a panel, balanced across age, gender, and income brackets to reflect target affluent and general‑homeowner segments.. Measure: Primary outcome: purchase intent (binary) and WTP (7‑point). Secondary outcome: self‑reported importance of trust vs status in purchase decision.. Predictions: T1: Trust‑framing group will show higher purchase intent and WTP than status‑framing group.; T2: Status‑framing group will show higher purchase intent and WTP than trust‑framing group.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between trust and status conditions is ≥ 10 percentage points, conclude the framing condition with the higher intent is more likely to drive demand. If the difference is ≤ 5 points, both conditions are equally plausible and further testing is needed. If the difference is ≥ 15 points, adopt the trust‑framing proposition (T1). If ≤ 5 points, adopt the status‑framing proposition (T2). If the WTP difference is ≥ €50, adopt the condition with the higher WTP as the value‑capture mechanism.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes Dräger’s professional safety credentials and trust in professional‑grade equipment. Begin with a limited launch targeting homeowners in regions where Dräger’s B2B reputation is already established, using existing distribution channels to capture margin on premium safety devices. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes Dräger’s professional safety credentials and trust in professional‑grade equipment. Begin with a limited launch targeting homeowners in regions where Dräger’s B2B reputation is already established, using existing distribution channels to capture margin on premium safety devices. Target customer: Affluent homeowners and safety‑conscious consumers who value proven professional‑grade safety equipment.. Value proposition: A Dräger’s consumer product that leverages the same sensor technology used by police, fire services, and industry, marketed as a safe, reliable home safety solution, allowing premium pricing and margin capture.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (Trust vs Status Framing) to validate whether trust‑framing drives higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than status‑framing. If the test confirms a ≥ 10‑point difference in purchase intent,. Uncertainty: The extent to which consumers actually trust Dräger’s professional reputation and are willing to pay a premium for home use remains uncertain. Evidence from the Consumer Messaging Test will resolve this.. Would change if: If the test shows the status‑framing condition outperforms trust by at least 10 percentage points, the recommendation would shift toward a status‑framed consumer proposition.; If willingness to pay differences are not significant (e.g., ≥ €50), the recommendation would remain focused on trust‑framed premium positioning.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for home safety devices across multiple channels, the recommendation could be updated to explore broader consumer expansion.. T1: Home ice maker demand is driven by convenience and the desire for fresh, chewable ice, not by a need for commercial-grade output. Consumers purchase ice machines to satisfy personal cravings for nugget ice, and they are willing to pay a premium for a product that delivers that experience at home. Who benefits: Residential consumers seeking convenient, high-quality ice for beverages and food preparation.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers shift from buying ice from stores or using ice tongs to owning a dedicated home machine because it eliminates the hassle and provides consistent, chewable ice on demand.. How value is captured: Hoshizaki can capture value by selling premium-priced countertop models with advanced features (e.g., nugget ice, smart controls) through direct sales and retail channels, leveraging its existing brand and distribution network.. Assumptions: Consumers perceive home ice machines as a convenience product rather than a commercial-grade fleet item.; Willingness to pay exceeds the cost of a standard commercial unit due to convenience and brand perception.; Distribution channels (direct sales, retail) can reach individual buyers effectively.. Predictions: A survey of residential consumers would show a higher purchase intent for a home ice machine than for a commercial-grade fleet unit.; Sales of premium-priced countertop models would exceed sales of standard commercial units in the same market.; Consumer reviews would emphasize convenience and taste as primary purchase drivers..

T2: Home ice maker demand is driven by a need for commercial-grade output and fleet efficiency, not by convenience or personal cravings. Businesses and institutions purchase ice machines to meet production or service requirements, and they seek high-output, reliable units that can be serviced and maintained. Who benefits: Commercial buyers (restaurants, hotels, dairies, food service providers) needing consistent, large-volume ice.. Why behaviour changes: These buyers shift from using ice tongs or store-bought ice to owning a dedicated machine because it reduces labor costs, ensures consistent product quality, and meets regulatory or service standards.. How value is captured: Hoshizaki can capture value by offering high-output, durable commercial units with advanced service support, and by selling through existing commercial distribution channels.. Assumptions: Commercial buyers prioritize output capacity and reliability over convenience.; There is a measurable demand for units that can serve multiple points of service.; Service and maintenance capabilities are critical to purchase decisions.. Predictions: A survey of commercial buyers would show higher purchase intent for high-output units than for premium-priced countertop models.; Sales of commercial-grade fleet units would exceed sales of premium-priced consumer models in the same market.; Buyers would emphasize serviceability and maintenance support as key purchase criteria..

Test "Consumer vs Commercial Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two message conditions: (A) convenience-driven home ice machine (nugget ice, on-demand convenience) or (B) commercial-grade fleet unit (high output, reliability, service). They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and to state the primary reason for choosing the product.. Sample: 300 residential consumers (150 per condition) and 200 commercial buyers (100 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1-7) and primary reason for choosing the product.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and primary reason of convenience for the convenience message.; T2: Higher purchase intent and primary reason of commercial output for the commercial message.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the convenience message is at least 1.5 points higher than for the commercial message (i.e., >= 5.5 out of 7) and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points or not statistically significant, conclude T2 is supported. If both conditions show similar intent, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home CPR Training" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group A (safety messaging) receives a home CPR training kit marketed as a safety product for family preparedness; Group B (digital integration) receives the same kit marketed as part of a digital health ecosystem (e.g., fitness app, insurance wellness program); Group C (control) receives no product. All participants are asked to indicate their willingness to pay (WTP) in euros and to report their likelihood to purchase the product on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 500 health-conscious adults recruited from an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and geographic regions.. Measure: Primary measure: average willingness to pay (WTP) in euros. Secondary measure: purchase intent (likelihood to purchase on a 7-point scale).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group B and Group C.; T2: Group B will show higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group A and Group C.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for Group A is at least 20% higher than Group B and at least 20% higher than Group C, proceed to develop a safety-focused consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 20% in either direction, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 10% in either direction, conduct a larger, more detailed test.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

T1: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is positioned as a safety and preparedness product for families, because they view CPR as a life-saving skill they should be able to perform in emergencies. Who benefits: Individual homeowners and their families who want to be prepared for cardiac emergencies.. Why behaviour changes: Growing public awareness of home cardiac arrests and the desire to be prepared for emergencies creates a perceived need for accessible, at-home training.. How value is captured: Laerdal can sell premium-priced home training kits directly to consumers, generate recurring revenue through optional add-ons (e.g., family training sessions), and build a brand of personal preparedness.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay for home CPR training if it is marketed as a safety product.; The market size for home CPR training is large enough to support a differentiated consumer proposition.; Laerdal can reach consumers through existing channels (e.g., online, retail) without significant new investment.. Predictions: If offered a home CPR training kit, a measured percentage of target homeowners will purchase it within 12 weeks.; Purchase intent will be higher among homeowners who report concern about home cardiac arrests compared to those who do not.; Repeat purchase or subscription rates will be higher for families who receive additional training resources..

T2: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is marketed as a health insurance or employer wellness benefit, because they view it as a cost-effective way to meet insurance or workplace requirements. Who benefits: Insurance companies, employers, and individual policyholders who need to meet coverage or wellness criteria.. Why behaviour changes: Insurance and employer mandates require employees or policyholders to complete CPR training, creating a demand for accessible, affordable home training that meets compliance.. How value is captured: Laerdal can sell training kits through insurance or HR channels, charge a premium for compliance-focused packaging, and generate recurring revenue from optional training extensions.. Assumptions: Insurance and employer requirements for CPR training exist and are enforceable.; Consumers are willing to purchase training kits as a compliance solution rather than a personal safety product.; Laerdal can partner with insurers or HR departments to reach target buyers.. Predictions: If offered a home CPR training kit as a compliance product, a measured percentage of target homeowners will purchase it within 12 weeks.; Purchase intent will be higher among homeowners who receive training through their insurance or workplace compared to those who purchase for personal reasons.; Repeat purchase rates will be higher for families who receive training as part of a compliance program..

Test "Home CPR Training Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Recruit 500 homeowners (300 per arm) who have expressed interest in home safety products. Randomly assign participants to one of two messaging conditions: (A) safety/ preparedness message emphasizing personal preparedness for home emergencies; (B) compliance/ insurance message emphasizing meeting insurance or employer requirements. After viewing a product description, participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Sample: 500 homeowners (300 per arm) screened via an online panel to ensure demographic diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay (EUR) for each messaging condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the safety/ preparedness condition compared to the compliance condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the compliance/ insurance condition compared to the safety condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the safety condition is at least 10 points higher than in the compliance condition (i.e., safety ≥ compliance + 10), proceed to develop a consumer proposition focused on personal preparedness. If compliance ≥ safety + 10, proceed to develop a consumer proposition focused on insurance/ employer compliance. If neither condition meets the threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. The evidence shows Laerdal already offers home CPR training (CPR Anytime) and donates infant kits, but it does not demonstrate consumer demand or willingness to pay. The proposed messaging test (X1) is the next step to validate whether safety/ preparedness messaging drives purchase intent. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. The evidence shows Laerdal already offers home CPR training (CPR Anytime) and donates infant kits, but it does not demonstrate consumer demand or willingness to pay. The proposed messaging test (X1) is the next step to validate whether safety/ preparedness messaging drives purchase intent. Target customer: Homeowners who have expressed interest in home safety products and are concerned about home cardiac emergencies.. Value proposition: A home CPR training kit positioned as a personal preparedness product, offering flexible, at-home learning with optional family training resources.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the Home CPR Training Messaging Test (X1) to compare purchase intent and willingness to pay under safety/ preparedness versus compliance/ insurance messaging.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market for home CPR training and the actual willingness to pay are unknown. The test will resolve whether safety/ preparedness messaging drives demand.. Would change if: If the messaging test shows the compliance/ insurance condition achieving purchase intent at least 10 points higher than the safety condition, we would shift focus to an insurance/ employer compliance proposition.; If neither condition meets the threshold, we would conclude insufficient evidence to justify investment in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
“Heating systems in Europe are unique and have a variety of hardware and software requirements that make it challenging to build for the diverse set of homes,” Google’s post states.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Test "Digital Messaging Test: SEAI vs Premium Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Run a targeted online ad campaign with two versions: Version A presents Kingspan insulation as a SEAI‑backed, grant‑simplified solution; Version B presents the same product as a premium, high‑performance insulation with a price premium. Track click‑through and purchase conversion rates for each version.. Sample: 2,000 UK homeowners recruited via social media and email lists, split equally between Version A and Version B.. Measure: Conversion rate (purchases) and average willingness‑to‑pay (WTP) for each version.. Predictions: T1: Version A will achieve a higher conversion rate and WTP than Version B because homeowners are motivated by public funding and grant simplicity.; T2: Version B will achieve a higher conversion rate and WTP than Version A because homeowners value premium performance and are willing to pay more.. Decision rule: If Version A’s conversion rate is at least 10 percentage points higher than Version B, conclude T1 is supported. If Version B’s conversion rate is at least 10 percentage points higher than Version A, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 10 percentage points, neither theory is conclusively supported and further testing is needed.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes the SEAI grant‑simplified, government‑backed process, while also highlighting premium performance. Use the One Stop Shop model to capture volume sales and leverage public funding to lower customer upfront cost. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes the SEAI grant‑simplified, government‑backed process, while also highlighting premium performance. Use the One Stop Shop model to capture volume sales and leverage public funding to lower customer upfront cost. Target customer: UK homeowners undertaking home energy upgrades, particularly those who are aware of and eligible for SEAI grants or building code requirements.. Value proposition: A trusted, government‑backed insulation solution that simplifies the grant application process and delivers proven thermal performance, making upgrades affordable and compliant.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed digital messaging test (Version A vs Version B) to measure conversion rates and willingness‑to‑pay, and use the results to decide whether to scale the premium positioning or maintain the grant‑focused approach.. Uncertainty: The extent to which homeowners actually use the SEAI grant process and their willingness to pay a premium for performance remain uncertain. Additionally, the competitive landscape and retailer distribution could affect adoption.. Would change if: If the test shows Version B (premium positioning) achieving a conversion rate at least 10 percentage points higher than Version A, we would shift focus to premium positioning.; If new evidence shows that homeowners are not aware of or do not trust the SEAI grant process, we would reconsider the grant‑focused proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Differentiated vs Branded Ice Machine Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to view either a differentiated ice machine (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling) or a branded ice machine (e.g., Scotsman Brilliance). They are then asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 U.S. adults aged 25–45 who have purchased an ice machine in the past 12 months, recruited via an online panel.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each product.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the differentiated unit than for the branded unit.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the branded unit than for the differentiated unit.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the differentiated and branded units is at least 1.5 points (e.g., differentiated intent ≥ 7.5 and branded intent ≤ 6), conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is at least 1.5 points in favor of the branded unit, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., nugget ice or easy refilling) rather than a brand-led premium offering. The evidence shows existing consumer interest in countertop ice machines and the ability to differentiate through convenience and novelty, which aligns with T1. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., nugget ice or easy refilling) rather than a brand-led premium offering. The evidence shows existing consumer interest in countertop ice machines and the ability to differentiate through convenience and novelty, which aligns with T1. Value proposition: A differentiated ice machine that delivers a unique, convenient experience (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling) that cannot be obtained from existing commercial or generic models, allowing Hoshizaki to capture value through licensing, premium. events.text: Objective: Determine whether Testo SE & Co. KGaA should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current B2B portable and stationary measuring instruments, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Current consumer reach is unknown; must be discovered from public sources.; Any new proposition must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive advantage.; Investment decision must consider risk, resource allocation, and potential impact on existing B2B operations.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home DIY, small business, or consumer health monitoring) with a new product or service model.; 2) Expand the existing B2B product line into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused accessories or services).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B market and existing product portfolio.; 4) Change the route to market for existing B2B products to reach consumers directly (e.g., e‑commerce, subscription services) without altering the core product.; 5) Target a different customer group within the B2B segment (e.g., small trades, individual contractors) with a differentiated proposition..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Testo portable measuring instruments for home energy efficiency and condensation checks if they view them as a transparent, independent verification tool that reduces uncertainty about energy performance and damp damage. Who benefits: Energy-conscious homeowners, homeowners concerned about condensation damage, and potential partner insurance or building inspection firms.. Why behaviour changes: Growing awareness of rising heating bills and condensation issues creates a demand for accurate, independent verification of a property’s energy performance and damp health, prompting homeowners to seek tools that provide clear, credibleAss. How value is captured: Testo can capture value by selling higher‑margin portable devices directly to consumers or through retail partners, while also enabling service contracts for verification reports and potential licensing for third‑party compliance services.. Assumptions: Consumers perceive current DIY checks as unreliable or insufficient.; Energy‑efficiency and condensation concerns are sufficiently widespread to justify new purchase behavior.; A differentiated proposition (e.g., a portable device with clear results and certification) can differentiate Testo from existing tools and services.; Retail or online channels are accessible to target consumers.. Predictions: In a test offering a consumer‑focused Testo device to homeowners, purchase intent will exceed 10% among surveyed households.; Surveyed homeowners will cite energy efficiency or condensation as a primary reason for purchase.; Sales of the new device will be concentrated in regions with high reported energy‑efficiency concerns (e.g., UK, Germany)..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Testo portable measuring instruments for home energy efficiency and condensation checks if they trust the brand as a professional-grade, independent authority that provides clear, actionable results, because they value credibility and reliability over price. Who benefits: Homeowners who prioritize trust and professional validation in home energy performance and damp health decisions.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers are increasingly skeptical of DIY claims and seek evidence from trusted sources. A brand known for professional-grade accuracy and independent certification reduces perceived risk and builds confidence in the results.. How value is captured: Testo can capture value by positioning premium-priced portable devices as professional-grade tools, selling through specialized retail or online channels, and offering subscription services for verification reports and compliance support.. Assumptions: Consumers associate professional-grade accuracy with higher cost.; Brand trust is a primary purchase driver for home energy and damp-related products.; A differentiated proposition can communicate professional credibility effectively.; Retail or online channels can reach the target consumer base.. Predictions: In a test offering a consumer-focused Testo device priced above standard portable tools, purchase intent will be driven by trust in professional credibility rather than price.; Surveyed homeowners will cite trust in the brand as the top reason for choosing Testo over competitors.; Sales will be concentrated in regions where professional reputation is already established (e.g., Germany, UK)..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Energy Efficiency vs Professional Trust" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and purchase intent measurement.. Sample: 500 UK homeowners (300 per arm) recruited via a panel to match demographic distribution of target regions.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and stated primary reason (energy efficiency vs professional trust). Secondary measure: willingness to pay (WTP) for a differentiated Testo device.. Predictions: T1: Homeowners exposed to energy‑efficiency messaging will have higher purchase intent and will cite energy efficiency as the primary reason, while those exposed to professional trust messaging will have lower intent.; T2: Homeowners exposed to professional trust messaging will have higher purchase intent and will cite trust in the brand as the primary reason, while those exposed to energy‑efficiency messaging will have lower intent.. Decision rule: If purchase intent for the energy‑efficiency arm exceeds professional trust arm by at least 10 percentage points, proceed with a differentiated energy‑efficiency proposition. If the difference is less than 5 points, consider a trust‑based proposition. If both arms are below 5 points, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners concerned about energy efficiency and condensation, using a portable device that provides transparent, independent verification. Begin with a limited pilot in regions with high energy‑efficiency concerns (e.g., UK, Germany) to test purchase intent and willingness to pay. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners concerned about energy efficiency and condensation, using a portable device that provides transparent, independent verification. Begin with a limited pilot in regions with high energy‑efficiency concerns (e.g., UK, Germany) to test purchase intent and willingness to pay. Target customer: Energy‑conscious homeowners and homeowners concerned about condensation damage who need accurate, independent verification of their property's energy performance and damp health.. Value proposition: A Testo portable device that delivers clear, independent results for energy efficiency and condensation checks, enabling homeowners to make informed decisions and potentially access service contracts for verification reports.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (or a similar pilot) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for an energy‑efficiency‑focused proposition.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and the specific willingness to pay for a differentiated device are uncertain. Evidence of strong consumer demand and brand trust is limited to public sources.. Would change if: If the Consumer Messaging Test shows purchase intent below 5% or if willingness to pay is negligible, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of no expansion.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for professional-grade credibility (e.g., high trust in the brand), the recommendation would shift toward a trust‑based proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.
Today, more than 350,000 cardiac arrests occur outside of hospitals in the United States annually. Nearly three out of four of those cardiac arrests happen in homes.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

T1: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is marketed as a personal health responsibility and delivered through a trusted brand, because they view CPR as a life-saving skill they should learn themselves. Who benefits: Individual consumers who want to be prepared for cardiac emergencies and feel responsible for their family safety.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers see CPR training as a personal responsibility and a way to gain confidence and control over emergency situations, they are more likely to purchase and complete the training.. How value is captured: Laerdal can capture value through direct-to-consumer sales of home training kits, subscription models for ongoing updates, and premium pricing justified by the personal health benefit.. Assumptions: Consumers perceive CPR training as a personal health responsibility rather than a professional training requirement.; A trusted brand can effectively communicate the personal health benefit of home CPR training.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for a product that directly improves their ability to save lives.. Predictions: Consumers will show higher purchase intent and actual purchase rates when the product is marketed as a personal health responsibility.; Purchase rates will be higher for kits marketed by established health brands compared to generic marketing.; Consumers will report higher perceived benefit and confidence in performing CPR after completing the training..

T2: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is integrated into existing consumer health routines and recommended by trusted health authorities, because they are already engaged in health-related activities and seek convenience and validation. Who benefits: Health-conscious consumers who already purchase fitness, wellness, and home safety products, and who value recommendations from trusted health organizations.. Why behaviour changes: If home CPR training is positioned as a convenient, everyday health habit and endorsed by recognized health authorities, consumers are more likely to adopt it as part of their routine rather than as a one-time purchase.. How value is captured: Laerdal can capture value through cross-selling existing consumer health products, subscription models for updates, and premium pricing justified by the convenience and authority endorsement.. Assumptions: Consumers are already engaged in health-related activities and are open to new health products.; Trust in health authorities (e.g., AHA, CDC) influences purchase decisions.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for products that fit their existing health routines.. Predictions: Consumers will show higher purchase intent and actual purchase rates when the product is marketed as part of a broader health routine and endorsed by trusted authorities.; Purchase rates will be higher for products marketed through existing consumer health channels (e.g., online retailers, wellness apps).; Consumers will report higher satisfaction and continued use when the product is integrated into their existing health habits..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home CPR Training" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging conditions. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=300). They are randomly assigned to one of three conditions: (1) Personal health responsibility messaging (emphasizing individual preparedness and family safety); (2) Health routine integration messaging (emphasizing convenience and alignment with existing health habits); (3) Authority endorsement messaging (emphasizing endorsement by trusted health authorities). Participants are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay for the product.. Sample: 300 health-conscious adults recruited via an online panel, balanced across the three conditions.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price willingness to pay for the home CPR training kit.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the personal health responsibility condition compared to the other two conditions.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the health routine integration condition compared to the other two conditions.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the personal health responsibility condition is at least 10 points higher than in the health routine integration condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T1 is supported and the recommendation is to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on personal health responsibility. If the average purchase intent in the health routine integration condition is at least 10 points higher than in the personal health responsibility condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T2 is supported and the recommendation is to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on health routine integration. If neither condition shows a significant difference, the recommendation is to maintain the current B2B focus.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for home CPR training that emphasizes personal health responsibility and family safety, leveraging Laerdal’s trusted brand and existing home training kit (CPR Anytime). The proposition should be marketed through direct-to-consumer channels and include a subscription model for updates, justified by evidence of consumer demand for preparedness and willingness to pay a Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for home CPR training that emphasizes personal health responsibility and family safety, leveraging Laerdal’s trusted brand and existing home training kit (CPR Anytime). The proposition should be marketed through direct-to-consumer channels and include a subscription model for updates, justified by evidence of consumer demand for preparedness and willingness to pay a Target customer: Health-conscious individuals and families who view CPR training as a personal responsibility and are willing to invest in preparedness for cardiac emergencies.. Value proposition: A home CPR training kit that empowers individuals to learn lifesaving skills at their own pace, backed by a trusted brand and a subscription model for ongoing updates, offering both personal safety and peace of mind.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay under personal health responsibility messaging, and proceed with product development if the test confirms a significant advantage over other. Uncertainty: The actual purchase behavior of consumers and their willingness to pay for home CPR training remain uncertain. The test results will determine whether the personal health responsibility messaging generates sufficient demand to justify the $. Would change if: If the Consumer Messaging Test shows that health routine integration messaging generates higher purchase intent and willingness to pay, the recommendation would shift to a proposition focused on integrating CPR training into existing health; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for home CPR training through existing consumer health channels or if a competitor successfully launches a consumer-focused home CPR product, the recommendation would be to explore; If the test results are inconclusive or the purchase intent is below the threshold, the recommendation would remain to maintain the current B2B focus and conduct further market research.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. In this simulated warehouse test, a new label printer reduced packing errors slightly. Nothing about wearers or buyers was measured.

In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.
Today, more than 350,000 cardiac arrests occur outside of hospitals in the United States annually. Nearly three out of four of those cardiac arrests happen in homes.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

T1: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is marketed as a safety and preparedness product for families, because they view CPR as a life-saving skill they should be able to perform in emergencies. Who benefits: Individual homeowners and their families who want to be prepared for cardiac emergencies.. Why behaviour changes: Increased public awareness of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests and the availability of home training kits creates a perceived need for preparedness, prompting purchase.. How value is captured: Laerdal can capture value through direct-to-consumer sales of home training kits, subscription-based access to digital content, and premium pricing justified by safety messaging.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay for home CPR training kits.; Marketing can effectively communicate the safety and preparedness benefits of CPR training.; Distribution channels (e.g., online, retail) are accessible to target consumers.. Predictions: Surveyed homeowners will express intent to purchase a home CPR training kit at a price point above standard consumer health devices.; Sales of home CPR kits will increase in regions with higher out-of-hospital cardiac arrest rates.; Consumers will report higher perceived preparedness after receiving training..

T2: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is positioned as a health insurance or employer wellness benefit, because they view CPR training as a required or incentivized wellness activity. Who benefits: Insurance companies, employers, and individual policyholders who seek to meet wellness or compliance requirements.. Why behaviour changes: Insurance and employer wellness programs often require or recommend CPR training as part of health benefits, creating a structured pathway for purchase.. How value is captured: Laerdal can capture value through bulk sales to insurers and employers, subscription-based access to digital content, and premium pricing justified by compliance and wellness messaging.. Assumptions: Insurance and employer wellness programs cover or recommend home CPR training.; Consumers are motivated by cost savings or compliance rather than personal preparedness.; Distribution channels (e.g., B2B partners) are available for bulk sales.. Predictions: Insurance and employer wellness programs will increase demand for home CPR training kits.; Sales of home CPR kits will be concentrated in regions with high insurance and employer penetration.; Consumers will report higher purchase intent when offered through wellness program channels..

Franke Coffee Systems, a division of the Franke Group, is a world-leading developer and manufacturer of professional coffee machines. Headquartered in Aarburg, Switzerland, the company brings together Swiss engineering excellence, state-of-the-art technology, and profound coffee expertise. Around 900 employees, together with an optimized service and distribution network of more than 300 partners, support businesses in 80 countries.

In a press release, De’Longhi reported a positive performance across all regions, with sales in Europe particularly high following rising demand for professional fully automatic coffee machines and growing premiumisation among home consumers.

The appliance manufacturer said its La Marzocco and Eversys business group continues to strengthen its brand position in the semi-automatic professional machine and at-home coffee machine markets, with customers in the latter segment ‘increasingly attentive’ to prosumer equipment, such as the La Marzocco Linea Mini and De’Longhi’s bean-to-cup machine range.
Every Franke coffee machine comes equipped with an integrated and adjustable grinder, as well as the option of using pre-ground beans.
In February of 2020 the company announced that its previous consumer-oriented machine with flat 54-millimeter burrs, the Mahlkönig Vario Home, would be retired from the product line.
Features include: Electronic Touch with White display, a Water Tank Capacity of: 1.8 Litres, a Coffee Beans drawer capacity of: 200g and space for 1 or 2 cups.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Franke Coffee Systems should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its professional coffee machines, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home office, small retail, or travel) with unique features and branding.; 2) Expand the existing professional line into adjacent consumer segments (e.g., semi‑automatic machines for home use) without a differentiated proposition.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on professional coffee machines and existing distribution channels.; 4) Partner with or license the professional technology to consumer brands rather than selling under Franke's own brand..

Why behaviour changes: Consumers increasingly seek products that reflect quality and heritage, and they are willing to pay more for perceived superior performance.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium-priced Franke machine at a higher price point, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard-priced machine.; Consumers will report higher satisfaction and willingness to recommend the product compared to a standard-priced alternative..

T2: Home consumers will adopt Franke coffee machines if they perceive them as a convenient, all-in-one solution that integrates grinding, brewing, and storage, reducing the need for multiple appliances and saving time. Why behaviour changes: Consumers prioritize time-saving and space efficiency, especially in small homes or offices where multiple devices are impractical.. How value is captured: Franke can capture value through bundled pricing, subscription models for consumables, and premium pricing for integrated features.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for a single, integrated machine.; The integrated grinding and brewing functionality is perceived as a significant advantage.; Franke can effectively communicate the convenience benefit to consumers.. Predictions: In a test offering a bundled Franke machine with integrated grinding and brewing, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard-priced machine.; Consumers will report higher convenience and lower perceived effort compared to a standard-priced alternative..

Test "Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants view one of two product descriptions for a Franke coffee machine (premium positioning vs convenience positioning) and are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay. A control group sees no description.. Sample: 300 adult consumers interested in coffee, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Premium group will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than convenience group.; T2: Convenience group will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than premium group.. Decision rule: If premium group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and its average willingness to pay ≥ €150, proceed to develop a premium consumer proposition. If convenience group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and its average willingness to pay ≥ €150, develop a convenience‑focused proposition. If neither group meets its threshold, do not expand.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Sample: 300 adult homeowners in Germany, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions (premium or sustainability).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and top reason for choosing the product.. Predictions: T1: Premium condition will yield a purchase intent score at least 1.5 points higher than the sustainability condition.; T2: Sustainability condition will yield a purchase intent score at least 1.5 points higher than the premium condition.. Decision rule: If the premium condition's mean score is at least 1.5 points higher than the sustainability condition's mean score, conclude that premium messaging drives higher purchase intent and recommend developing a differentiated consumer proposition emphasizing hygiene and space savings. If the sustainability condition's mean score is at least 1.5 points higher, conclude that sustainability messaging drives higher purchase intent and recommend a sustainability‑focused proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, indicate uncertainty and suggest further testing.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Personal Responsibility vs. Mandate" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners (n=300). Each participant sees one of two product descriptions for a home safety device (a gas detector) and is asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay. The two descriptions differ only in framing: Condition A frames the device as a personal protective equipment for everyday home use, emphasizing individual responsibility. Condition B frames it as a health insurance or employer mandate requirement, emphasizing compliance. Participants are randomly assigned to see either condition.. Sample: 300 homeowners recruited from an online panel, balanced across gender and age. Randomly assigned to see either Condition A or Condition B.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay in Condition A (personal responsibility framing) compared to Condition B.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay in Condition B (mandate framing) compared to Condition A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average purchase intent between Condition A and Condition B is at least 1.5 points (e.g., Condition A ≥ 6.5 and Condition B ≤ 5.0), conclude the framing that aligns with the theory is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants view a product description of a Franke coffee machine (identical spec) and are offered two price points: a premium price 20% above a comparable entry-level machine and a standard price. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10) and to rank quality and convenience importance.. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and importance ranking (quality vs convenience) for each price point.. Predictions: T1: Premium price will generate purchase intent at least 15% higher than standard price, and quality will be ranked higher than convenience.; T2: Convenience message will generate purchase intent at least 15% higher than premium price, and convenience will be ranked higher than quality.. Decision rule: If premium price purchase intent ≥ 15% points higher than standard price AND quality ranking ≥ convenience ranking, proceed to develop a premium consumer proposition. If convenience message purchase intent ≥ 15% points higher than premium price AND convenience ranking ≥ quality ranking, develop a convenience‑focused proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Value proposition: A premium‑priced Franke machine that combines professional‑grade quality, modern design, and convenience features (e.g., integrated grinder, pre‑ground beans, time‑saving automation) to meet the needs of busy consumers.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test (300 participants, two price points, purchase intent and importance ranking) to determine whether consumers will pay a premium for quality or convenience.. Uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay a premium price for Franke machines is unknown; the test will provide data on purchase intent and importance rankings. Additionally, the competitive landscape and consumer price sensitivity remain uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the premium price is at least 15% lower than for the standard price, indicating insufficient demand for a premium proposition.; If the test shows purchase intent for the convenience message is at least 15% higher than for the premium price, indicating convenience is the primary driver.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for Franke machines in specific segments, such as home office or small retail, the recommendation could shift toward expanding into those segments.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for features that directly support their diet.; Marketing can effectively link the scale to health and wellness messaging.; Direct sales can reach individual buyers effectively.. Test "Precision vs Health Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from a panel of home cooks and health-conscious individuals. They view two product descriptions of a differentiated digital kitchen scale: one emphasizing precision for accurate ingredient measurement (T1) and one emphasizing health and wellness for portion control and carbohydrate counting (T2). After viewing the description, participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay (a numeric price).. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) from a panel of home cooks and health-conscious individuals, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (numeric).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for the precision-focused description.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for the health-focused description.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the two conditions is at least 10 percentage points and the health-focused condition achieves a willingness to pay at least 15% above the precision condition, proceed with the health-focused consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 10 points or the health condition does not meet the willingness-to-pay threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.
