Test "Consumer Preference Test: Convenience vs Sustainability" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Group A sees a description of a compact, high-performance scrubber marketed as convenient for small spaces and tight budgets. Group B sees the same product described as sustainable, eco-friendly, and water-efficient. Both groups see price points and a call-to-action to purchase. The test measures purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (maximum price).. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two groups (150 per group). Recruitment targets homeowners and small business owners with limited space.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and maximum willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary measure: stated primary purchase driver (convenience vs sustainability).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If Group A purchase intent exceeds Group B by at least 10 percentage points and its average willingness to pay is at least 20% higher, conclude T1 is supported. If Group B purchase intent exceeds Group A by at least 10 percentage points and its average willingness to pay is at least 20% higher, conclude T2 is supported. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience and small-space performance, targeting homeowners and small businesses with limited floor-cleaning areas. Use premium pricing and direct-to-consumer channels to capture higher margins. Target customer: Homeowners and small business owners with limited space who currently use mops or traditional scrubbers for small areas.. Value proposition: A compact, high-performance scrubber that delivers superior cleanliness with minimal effort and footprint, offering a convenient and affordable alternative to traditional cleaning methods.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Preference Test (Convenience vs Sustainability) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay. If the test meets the decision thresholds, proceed to develop and launch the consumer product; otherwise, reassess. Uncertainty: The willingness of consumers to pay a premium for convenience and small-space performance is uncertain. Additionally, the competitive landscape and the size of the consumer market remain unknown.. Would change if: If the test shows Group B (sustainability-focused) achieving higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Group A, the recommendation would shift toward a sustainability-focused consumer proposition.; If the test fails to meet the thresholds or shows no significant difference, the investment would be reconsidered, and further evidence would be sought.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners and small commercial users. Each participant sees one of two product descriptions for a differentiated undercounter dishwasher: (A) premium, space-saving messaging emphasizing convenience and multiple task capability; (B) sustainability messaging emphasizing water and energy efficiency. After viewing the description, participants indicate their willingness to pay a premium (willingness-to-pay) and their intent to purchase on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) recruited from a panel of homeowners and small commercial users in Germany and Austria.. Measure: Willingness-to-pay (willingness to pay a premium) and purchase intent (on a 7-point scale).. Predictions: T1: Higher willingness-to-pay and purchase intent in the premium condition compared to the sustainability condition.; T2: Higher willingness-to-pay and purchase intent in the sustainability condition compared to the premium condition.. Decision rule: If the premium condition yields a mean willingness-to-pay at least 1.5 points higher than the sustainability condition and a mean purchase intent at least 1.5 points higher, conclude T1 is supported. If the sustainability condition yields a mean willingness-to-pay at least 1.5 points higher than the premium condition and a mean purchase intent at least 1.5 points higher, conclude T2 is supported. If neither difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Test "Consumer vs Professional Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a consumer-focused message emphasizing convenience, compact size, and low upfront cost; Group B sees a professional-focused message emphasizing durability, high performance, and cost savings for contractors. Both groups view a product description of a compact scrubber priced at $300.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 homeowners and small‑business owners (recruited via online panels) and 250 professional cleaning contractors (recruited via industry forums).. Measure: Purchase intent measured as a binary response: "Would you purchase this compact scrubber?" and willingness to pay (WTP) in a 1‑10‑point scale.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Group B, indicating consumer demand for a differentiated proposition.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Group A, indicating professional demand for a differentiated proposition.. Decision rule: If purchase intent in Group A is at least 15 percentage points higher than in Group B, conclude T1 is supported. If purchase intent in Group B is at least 15 percentage points higher than in Group A, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 5 percentage points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Winterhalter Gastronom GmbH should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current commercial dishwashers and glasswashers, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeframe for any proposed experiment.; Current reach to individual buyers is unknown; must be discovered.; Any investment must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and ability to capture value.; Alternatives include product redesign, new distribution route, targeting a different customer group, or no expansion.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home kitchen dishwashers) with dedicated branding, marketing, and sales channels.; 2) Expand the existing commercial product line into adjacent consumer segments without differentiation (e.g., add a consumer‑grade glasswasher).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial dishwashers and glasswashers, possibly deepening existing B2B relationships.; 4) Change the route to buyers: partner with retailers or online platforms to reach consumers directly, leveraging existing distribution networks.; 5) Target a different customer group: shift focus to small restaurants, cafes, or hotel chains rather than large commercial facilities..

Measure: Primary measure: self‑reported top purchase driver (appearance/customization vs energy efficiency). Secondary measure: stated willingness to pay (WTP) for the customizable model.. Predictions: T1: Group A will report appearance/customization as the top driver and higher WTP for the customizable model.; T2: Group B will report energy efficiency as the top driver and higher WTP for the energy‑efficient model.. Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home Cleaning Proposition" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners and small business owners. They are shown two product descriptions of a differentiated consumer floor-cleaning machine (e.g., a compact scrubber for small spaces). One description emphasizes premium positioning (e.g., 'Convenient, high-performance cleaning for small areas') and the other emphasizes safety-critical features (e.g., 'Child-safe, slip-resistant design for safe home cleaning'). Participants are then asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) to ensure statistical power and detect a 5‑point difference in purchase intent.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the premium positioning condition compared to the safety condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the safety condition compared to the premium positioning condition.. Decision rule: If the premium positioning condition achieves a purchase intent score at least 5 points higher than the safety condition, conclude T1 is supported. If the safety condition achieves a purchase intent score at least 5 points higher than the premium condition, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 5 points, the test is inconclusive and further research is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes premium positioning and convenience for small home cleaning tasks, leveraging Tennant’s existing distribution network to reach individual buyers. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes premium positioning and convenience for small home cleaning tasks, leveraging Tennant’s existing distribution network to reach individual buyers. Target customer: Homeowners and small business owners seeking efficient, easy-to-use cleaning equipment for small spaces.. Value proposition: A compact, high-performance floor scrubber that delivers superior cleaning in tight areas, offering convenience and convenience without compromising performance, positioned as a premium, sustainable solution.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for premium positioning versus safety-critical features, and adjust messaging accordingly.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and the specific drivers of consumer purchase decisions (premium positioning, convenience, or safety) remain uncertain. The test will provide data to resolve this.. Would change if: If the test shows the safety condition achieving a purchase intent score at least 5 points higher than the premium condition, we would shift focus to safety-critical features and reconsider the premium positioning strategy.; If the test shows no significant difference in purchase intent between the two conditions, we would reconsider the investment in a differentiated consumer proposition and explore alternative routes to market.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer Preference Test: Space vs Sustainability Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from homeowners with limited kitchen space (≤15 sq ft). They view a product description of a Winterhalter undercounter dishwasher, then choose between two messaging conditions: (A) space-saving undercounter unit with multi-functional use; (B) sustainable eco-friendly product with lower carbon footprint. They also indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 300 homeowners (150 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and kitchen size.. Measure: Primary outcome: purchase intent (percentage choosing the respective condition). Secondary outcomes: average WTP (EUR) and self-reported importance of space savings vs sustainability.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will generate higher purchase intent than Condition B because space savings and multi-functional use are the primary purchase drivers.; T2: Condition B will generate higher purchase intent than Condition A because sustainability is the primary purchase driver.. Decision rule: If purchase intent for Condition A exceeds Condition B by ≥10 percentage points, conclude T1 is supported. If purchase intent for Condition B exceeds Condition A by ≥10 percentage points, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is <5 percentage points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

case.question: Should Laerdal Medical develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing resuscitation and healthcare-simulation training products? What evidence would justify that investment?

sources.excerpt: In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

T1: Home CPR training increases public awareness and willingness to intervene in cardiac arrest, leading individuals to purchase home training kits to prepare for emergencies. The perceived reduction of risk and the ability to act immediately create demand, which Laerdal can capture through direct-to-consumer sales of portable kits. Who benefits: Individual consumers who need to prepare for emergencies, and by extension, bystanders who might perform CPR in an emergency.. Why behaviour changes: Increased public awareness of the importance of bystander CPR and the availability of easy-to-use home kits lowers the perceived risk and creates a perceived benefit, prompting individuals to own the training device.. How value is captured: Laerdal would capture value through premium-priced home CPR kits sold directly to consumers, generating revenue beyond B2B training programs.. Assumptions: Consumers are aware of the importance of bystander CPR and are willing to invest in home training.; Home CPR kits are perceived as safe and effective for self-training.; Laerdal can reach and convert consumers effectively at a price point that justifies the investment.. Predictions: In regions with high public awareness of bystander CPR, home CPR kit purchases will be higher than in regions with low awareness.; Consumers will indicate a willingness to pay a premium for a home CPR kit compared to a standard CPR manikin..

T2: Consumers adopt home CPR training because it is marketed as a health and wellness product, aligning with personal fitness and self-care trends. This positioning attracts health-conscious individuals who view CPR training as part of their lifestyle, leading to purchase decisions driven by perceived personal benefit rather than emergency preparedness. Who benefits: Health-conscious consumers who seek to enhance personal wellness and are willing to invest in home health devices.. Why behaviour changes: The integration of CPR training into a wellness narrative creates a personal benefit that motivates purchase, as consumers associate learning a life-saving skill with overall health improvement.. How value is captured: Laerdal would capture value through premium-priced home wellness kits sold directly to consumers, leveraging existing consumer marketing channels to reach health-conscious audiences.. Assumptions: Consumers associate CPR training with personal health and wellness benefits.; Marketing can effectively frame CPR training as a lifestyle product.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for a product positioned as part of their wellness routine.. Predictions: In markets where wellness and self-care are prioritized, home CPR kit purchases will be higher than in markets where health concerns are less prominent.; Consumers will express higher willingness to pay for a home CPR kit when marketed as a wellness product compared to a standard CPR manikin..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Emergency vs Wellness Framing" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel representing health-conscious and general consumers. Participants view a product description of a portable home CPR kit and are randomly assigned to one of two messaging conditions: (A) Emergency preparedness framing (emphasizes bystander CPR, life-saving skills, and family preparedness). (B) Wellness framing (emphasizes personal health, fitness, and lifestyle integration). After viewing the description, participants indicate their willingness to pay a premium (price sensitivity) and their intent to purchase (binary).. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) recruited from a health-conscious panel and a general consumer panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Willingness to pay premium (difference in price sensitivity between conditions) and purchase intent (binary).. Predictions: T1: Higher willingness to pay premium and higher purchase intent in the emergency framing condition compared to wellness framing.; T2: Higher willingness to pay premium and higher purchase intent in the wellness framing condition compared to emergency framing.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay premium for emergency framing exceeds wellness framing by at least €10 (or a 10% increase in purchase intent), proceed with developing a differentiated consumer proposition focused on emergency preparedness. If the difference is less than €10, the test is inconclusive and further market research is needed.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.
